newsitem.title: USA: Teacher's sexual affair with boy divides Seattle.
newsitem.headline: Teacher's sexual affair with boy divides Seattle.

text.p: In a case that has divided Seattle and raised questions of reverse gender bias, a 35-year-old teacher awaits sentencing on child rape charges for seducing a 13-year-old student and bearing his child.

Mary Kay LeTourneau, a mother of four and daughter of a conservative former California congressman, was a highly regarded grade school teacher until her arrest shocked the community in February. She pleaded guilty last week and said she still had romantic feelings for the boy.
The boy is now 14 and reportedly harbors similar feelings for the teacher he has known since the second grade. His mother is caring for the couple's baby girl born in May.
The case has become a prime topic of water-cooler conversation in Seattle, where many men have hinted they envy the young man his extracurricular experience with the attractive, blonde teacher.
Experts say such sentiments represent a clear case of reverse gender bias, noting there would be little sympathy for a male teacher who took liberties with a young girl.
"I have a name for them -- the Mrs. Robinsons," said Florence Wolfe, co-director of a Seattle treatment center for sex offenders, referring to the "older woman" in the 1967 movie "The Graduate."

"It is hard for people to accept that she should be held responsible for her acts," Wolfe said. "But it really does a lot of bad stuff to the kid's brain to be mixed up sexually with someone who's such a mentor."

After she pleaded guilty to two counts of second-degree child rape in King County Superior Court last week, LeTourneau was taken into custody as required by state law on sex offenders. She will be sentenced on Aug. 29.
Her attorney, David Gehrke, said LeTourneau "regrets her actions deeply."
"She did a horrible thing," he said. "But we all make mistakes. She's a very good person who did a very bad thing."

While the standard sentence for similar crimes ranges from about five to seven years, Gehrke will seek an alternative option that would mean no more than six months in jail if she successfully completes a treatment program.

Prosecutors have not decided what sentence to recommend at a hearing to be held in a jailhouse courtroom likely to be crowded with journalists from as far away as Japan who have inquired about the case.

The liaison between teacher and student, which lasted about six months, shattered two families and disrupted life at Shorewood Elementary School in Burien, a working-class suburb just south of Seattle.

Nick Latham, public information officer for the Highline School District, said there was "shock, disbelief," after LeTourneau was dismissed, while her students were angered at the system that took their teacher away literally overnight.
LeTourneau's husband, Steve, has filed for divorce and moved to Alaska with their four children, the oldest of whom is 12, after winning sole custody in court.
The 14-year-old boy has been kept in near-seclusion by his mother, who has said she was devastated when she learned of the sexual nature of the relationship.

In the latest twist, newspapers revealed that LeTourneau is the daughter of former conservative Republican Rep. John Schmitz of California, whose own career was destroyed by revelations he had a mistress and two illegitimate children in addition to seven children with his wife.
Schmitz, who once ran for president on a third-party ticket, had built his political reputation on strong support of conservative family values.
LeTourneau first met the boy when he was in her second-grade class and stayed in touch with him over the years, buying him art supplies and teaching him about music.
The bond became closer when LeTourneau moved up to sixth grade and the boy was in her class again, and the relationship turned sexual in the summer of 1996.
Through it all, the boy has maintained that he loves his former teacher.
"I want people to stop seeing me as a victim," he told The Seattle Times. "Mary didn't harm me in any way. Who are they to say I'm too young to know anything when they don't even know me?"
